what_its_for: Fexofenadine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy skin rashes (hives). It works by blocking histamine, the chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do NOT take fexofenadine with fruit juices such as orange juice, apple juice, or grapefruit juice, as these can reduce how well the medicine works. Use water only. If you are taking the orally disintegrating tablet, place it on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not swallow it whole.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: The usual dose is 60 mg twice a day OR 180 mg once a day. Children 2 to 11 years: The usual dose is 30 mg twice a day. Always follow the dose on your prescription label or the package directions. Do not take more than the recommended amount.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fexofenadine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication properly — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking fruit juices (orange, apple, or grapefruit juice) around the time you take this medicine — these can make fexofenadine less effective. Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox or Mylanta) within 15 minutes before or after taking fexofenadine, as they can also reduce how much medicine your body absorbs. Although fexofenadine is less likely to make you drowsy than older antihistamines, some people may still feel sleepy — use caution when driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek medical help right away if you experience: a serious allergic reaction (trouble breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe rash); fast or irregular heartbeat; dizziness or fainting; or if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of use. Also tell your doctor if you have kidney disease before taking this medicine, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
when_it_works: Fexofenadine usually starts working within 1 to 3 hours after you take it. You should notice improvement in your allergy symptoms such as less sneezing, itching, and runny nose within this time frame.
special_populations: Older adults and people with kidney problems may need a lower dose because their bodies clear the medicine more slowly — talk to your doctor or pharmacist. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should consult their doctor before using fexofenadine. For children under 2 years of age, do not use this medicine unless directed by a doctor.
